```{r}
#| label: load data
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)

h1data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h1_revised.csv")
# Make employment a factor again
h1data$Employment_group <- factor(h1data$Employment_group,
                                  levels = c("Full-time","Unemployed"))

h2data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h2_revised.csv")
```

## Hypothesis 1
Individualistic attitudes will be stronger among full-time employed individuals than unemployed individuals.

### Variables and descriptive statistics
- **Employment Status (`Employment_group`):** A categorical variable with two groups: Full Time and Unemployed.
- **Individualistic Attitudes(`ind_rev_mean`):** How strongly someone prioritizes personal rewards and goals over group welfare. The mean of reverse coded, available responses to (`Individualism_col_1`), (`Individualism_col_2`), and (`Individualism_col_4`). Each item ranges from 1 (Definitely Disagree) to 7 (Definitely Agree); higher scores indicate stronger individualistic attitudes. 

```{r}
#| label: h1-descriptives
# Count respondents in each group.
table(h1data$Employment_group)

# Summarize individualistic attitude scores separately for each group.
by(h1data$ind_rev_mean,h1data$Employment_group,summary)
```

### Graphs 

@fig-individualism shows the distribution of individualistic attitudes by employment status. The boxes represent the middle 50% of the data and quartiles. The whiskers represent the spread and range of the data.

```{r}
#| label: fig-individualism
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of individualistic attitudes, by empolyment status."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

h1BoxPlot <- ggplot(data = h1data,
                aes(x= Employment_group,
                    y = ind_rev_mean,
                    fill = Employment_group))+
  labs(x = "Employment Status",
       y = "Individualistic Attitudes",
       title = "Individualistic Attitudes Compared by Employment Status")+
  scale_x_discrete(labels = (c("Full Time", "Unemployed")))+
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(1,7),
    breaks = 1:7) +
  theme_gray(base_size=13) +
  geom_boxplot() 
h1BoxPlot
```
## H2
Gender-equality attitudes will be associated with daily time spent enhancing appearance.

### Variables and descriptive statistics
- **Gender Equality Attitude (`Gender_Equality_mean`):**  The mean of reverse coded, available responses to (`Gender_Equality_1`), (`Gender_Equality_2`), and (`Gender_Equality_3`). Each item ranges from 1 (Definitely Disagree) to 7 (Definitely Agree); higher scores indicate greater gender equality endorsement.
- **Daily time spent enhancing appearance(`appearance_time_sum`):** The sum of eight activity items in minutes per days. (`Time_A_makeup_1`), (`Time_A_hyg_1`), (`Time_A_cosm_1`), (`Time_A_exercise_1`), (`Time_A_hair_1`), (`Time_A_dress_1`), (`Time_A_diet_1`), (`Time_A_other_1`); higher means more time.

```{r}
#| label: h2-descriptives
summary(h2data[, c("Gender_Equality_mean", "appearance_time_sum")])
```
### Graph 
@fig-appearance shows the relationship between time spent on enhancing appearance and gender equality attitudes. Points are jittered to make overlapping responses easier to see; the recorded scores are unchanged. The line summarizes the linear trend.

```{r}
#| label: fig-appearance
#| fig-cap: "CTime spent enhancing appearance in relation to gender equality attitudes."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

h2JitterLinePlot <- ggplot(data = h2data,
                    aes(x=Gender_Equality_mean,
                        y=appearance_time_sum))+
    geom_jitter(width = .12,height=.04,alpha=.04,size = .6)+
    labs(x="Gender Equality Attitude Score",
       y="Total Time Spent on Appearance",
       title="Relationship between Gender Equality Attitudes and Time Spent on Appearance") +
  theme_gray(base_size = 18) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

h2JitterLinePlot
```

### Observed trend 

```{r}
#| label: correlation
r <- cor(h2data$Gender_Equality_mean, h2data$appearance_time_sum, use = "complete.obs")
round(r, 2)
```

The correlation was `{r} round(r, 2)`, indicating a weak negative association. Respondents who reported more egalitarian Gender Attitudes tended to reported less time spent on enhancing appearance.
